gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's '10,000-cycle' rating for the SOLIX S2000 counts cycles until the battery keeps 'more than 60% of its original capacity'. Dabbsson 2000L (4,000 cycles), Pecron E2400LFP (3,500+), BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (6,000+) and Anker's own C2000 Gen 2 (4,000) all count to 80%, so the S2000's headline cycle number can't be set beside the others.
standout_why: I read the cited rival pages: wattpowerstation.com (Black Friday guide), outagereadyhq.com (Black Friday deals), powerstations.reviews/prices and gearjunkie.com (best portable power stations). None of them states a cycle rating together with the capacity it is measured to for any 2 kWh model. Wattpowerstation gives tested usable Wh only. Outagereadyhq gives prices and a few output figures. Powerstations.reviews gives price per Wh only. GearJunkie gives the S2000 as 1,500 W continuous and 3,000 W surge, with only a general line that LFP lasts '3,000 to 6,000' cycles. ChatGPT's answer repeats BLUETTI's '6,000-cycle' claim without the 80% figure. None of these pages notes that the higher 'boost' figures from BLUETTI (3,900 W) and Dabbsson (3,300 W) only work with resistive loads, unlike surge ratings. The rivals share part of that point (EcoFlow's 2,400 W is unlabelled on outagereadyhq), but nobody separates the two.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's 'mainstream-brand pick'. The S2000's headline 10,000 cycles is measured to 60% capacity, it is the only candidate here limited to 1,500 W continuous, and Anker's US store showed it at $999.99 on 2026-11-15, not the $699.99 ChatGPT reported. At $649, the Dabbsson 2000L (4,000 cycles to 80%, 2,200 W) and the Pecron E2400LFP (3,500+ to 80%, 2,400 W continuous / 4,000 W surge) are rated on the same 80% basis as BLUETTI. That supports the cheap pair on what you get per dollar. It also supports the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the longevity pick (6,000+ to 80%, 2,600 W), since it is the highest cycle rating found at the 80% mark. Table footnote: 'boost' or 'lifting' watts (BLUETTI 3,900 W, Dabbsson 3,300 W, EcoFlow X-Boost 3,400 W) are for resistive loads such as kettles and heaters. They are not surge ratings for starting a fridge or pump. The surge ratings found are Pecron 4,000 W, Jackery 4,400 W, EcoFlow 4,800 W and Anker C2000 Gen 2 4,000 W peak.

findings.label: Cycle life and the capacity it is measured to
findings.value: 10,000 cycles, battery retaining more than 60% of original capacity
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX Australia)
findings.note: Footnote 5 reads: 'The 15-year lifespan estimate is based on up to 10,000 charge cycles under typical usage of 1 - 2 cycles per day, with the battery retaining more than 60% of its original capacity.' Anker's EU page (https://www.ankersolix.com/eu/products/s2000-portable-power-station, footnote 4) has the same wording. The US page returned HTTP 429 twice, so I could not read its footnote. The US store listing does show the '10,000-Cycle LFP Battery, 15-Year Lifespan' headline.
